question.leadin: Answer some questions about very badly named military operations.
question.text: Operations Breakfast, Lunch, Snack, Dinner, Supper, and Dessert were launched to bomb this country neighboring Vietnam during the Vietnam War.
question.answerHtml: Kingdom of Cambodia [or le Royaume du Cambodge, or Prĕəh Riəciənaacak Kampuciə; accept Democratic Kampuchea or Kâmpŭchéa Prâcheathippadey; accept Srok Khmae]
question.clue: This nation fought a long-running war with its neighbor, Vietnam, from 1979 to 1991, which had invaded in order to end the violent government of Pol Pot, the Khmer Rouge {KUH-MEER - ROOZ}.

swap.leadin: This woman won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize but could not accept it in person, as the ruling military junta held her under house arrest.
swap.text: Name this activist and politician who became State Counsellor of her country in 2016. Since her rise to power, she has been heavily criticized for her inaction against the persecution of the Rohingya people.
swap.answerHtml: Aung San Suu Kyi ([ong sahn soo chee], but be lenient) (prompt on “Suu” or “Kyi” alone)
swap.clue: She leads the National League for Democracy, which she formed after the 8888 Uprising to protest against General Ne Win's dictatorship.

question.text: The accusations of Duterte "death squads" come from when he was Mayor of Davao City on this Philippine island, the main home of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front.
question.clue: Historically, the Sulu Sultanate controlled large portions of this island's Zamboanga Peninsula.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Southeast Asian independence movements.
swap.text: David Marshall campaigned for the independence of this country. Reforms by its first leader, Lee Kwan Yew, made this city-state one of the four "Asian Tigers" with rapidly-growing economies.
swap.clue: HMS Prince of Wales led a naval group named Force Z assigned to protect this country that was destroyed by Japanese airstrikes prior to an invasion by Tomoyuki Yamashita's forces.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Chinese diaspora in Southeast Asia.
question.text: Chinese mining companies known as kongsi operated in this modern-day country before their suppression by the Dutch East Indies. This country is governed from Jakarta.
question.clue: A president of this country formulated a "New Order" to replace his predecessor's policy of "Guided Democracy."

swap.leadin: This leader converted a high school into the s21 ("s-twenty-one") prison.
swap.text: Name this man, who called himself "Brother Number One" while leading the Khmer Rouge. ("Kuh-mair roozh")
swap.clue: Relations between this man's government and its Eastern neighbor deteriorated during his rule, leading to a Vietnamese invasion that ousted him from power.

question.text: The Ayutthaya controlled land in this modern-day country. European traders who initially encountered the Ayutthaya called this country Siam.
question.clue: Its rulers used the Paknam Incident to create an irredentist nationalism later deployed by the Phibun government.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about anti-Communist activities in Southeast Asia.
swap.text: In this country, the Commonwealth of Nations fought a twelve-year civil war called "the Emergency" against communist guerillas. This country's native population is called the "bumiputra."
swap.clue: It's not the Soviet Union, but this country established the New Economic Policy to grant economic concessions to the majority ethnic group following the 13 May Incident.

question.leadin: Robert Olen Butler's A Good Scent From a Strange Mountain speaks to the unique struggles of immigrants from this country to the US.
question.text: Name this country, many of whose so-called "boat people" settled in the Gulf Coast.
question.clue: The Le Dynasty was nominally in control of this country for over 300 years.

swap.text: The Vietnamese invasion of Cambodia also allowed this communist movement in a neighboring country to establish a namesake "People's Democratic Republic" in 1975.
swap.clue: The book Man in the Region of Death was an account of this organization's prison camps by former RLG official Thongthip Rathanavilai, though unlike the Khmer Rouge this organization never established massive death camps.

question.text: 1. points) These twin towers in Kuala Lumpur took over the title of world's tallest building from the Sears Tower on their completion in 1996.

swap.text: The protest on Kent State was specifically directed against this decision announced by Richard Nixon on April 30, which controversially expanded the Vietnam War to another country.
swap.answerHtml: invasion of the Kingdom of Cambodia [or Cambodian campaign]
swap.answer: invasion of the Kingdom of Cambodia
swap.clue: The protestors killed in the Kent State shootings of 1970 were protesting this specific facet of the Vietnam War, which had been made public by President Nixon on April 30.

question.leadin: Name these plucky Brits with important dealings in Southeast Asia.
question.text: This Governor-General of Bencoolen negotiated with Hussein of Johor to establish a trading post, where he subsequently appointed William Farquhar ["FAR"-kwar] as First Resident.
question.clue: His methods allowed 3000 graves of the Naqada period to be assembled into successive orders.

swap.leadin: Groups called Kongsi were originally formed as guilds for industrial gold mines on this island.
swap.text: Name this Southeast Asian island where the Lanfang and Kengwei Kongsis resisted the Dutch and took advantage of trade opportunities with this island's Sultanates of Sambas and Landak.
swap.clue: James Brooke established a dynasty of "White Rajahs" who ruled Sarawak on this island.

question.leadin: You are a hpaya kyun ("PUH-yah CHOON"), one of many indentured servants that tend to Buddhist monks and religious property. Answer the following about your life.
question.text: Your job is to clean religious buildings like this oldest stupa in the world. Dhammazedi's bell was constructed to be situated at this pagoda built around eight strands of the Buddha's hair.
question.answerHtml: Shwedagon Pagoda [or Great Dagon Pagoda; accept Golden Dagon Pagoda; prompt on Golden Pagoda or Great Pagoda]
question.clue: According to a legend, the merchants Taphussa and Bhallika founded this location after receiving eight pieces of hair from Gautama Buddha.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the 30th of September Movement, whose most significant action, the murder of six generals, actually took place on October 1st, 1965.
swap.text: The military blamed this political party for the murders, using the 30th of September Movement as a pretext for the mass murder of its members. This party was subsequently banned in March 1966, and remains illegal today.
swap.clue: This party was exonerated of responsibility for a coup attempt in the "Cornell Paper" written by Benedict Anderson and Ruth McVey.

question.text: The second, or "restored" dynasty of this name, was the frst to re-unify Burma afer the fall of the Pagan kingdom and had its capital at Ava around 1606. The frst dynasty by this name arose in Burma under Mingyinyo near the end of the Ava kingdom and conquered the Mohnyin Shan peoples.

swap.text: With tacit approval from US ambassador Henry Cabot Lodge Jr., this man led a group of generals that overthrew and assassinated Diem in 1963. He later surrendered to communist forces in 1975 as South Vietnam's last president.

question.text: This monk's self-immolation, an act of protest against Diem, was captured by Malcolm Browne. In that picture, this man sits still in front of a car with its hood popped open as he burnt to death.

swap.leadin: Religious tensions in this country were exacerbated by the state-sponsored transmigration program, which made religious minorities feel that they would be overwhelmed by outsiders.
swap.text: Name this country where riots in Ambon led to the creation of Laskar Jihad during a religious conflict that displaced over half a million people between 1999 and 2002.
swap.clue: After Portugal announced the decolonization of Timor, this nation annexed the newly freed state.
